- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term trend shifts; if sentiment turns from negative to positive over 5+ days, increase forecast by 2–4% to reflect momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lag correction to forecast horizon.
